about_the_game:
In June, 1951, a team of researchers were sent from the Desert National Wildlife Range to the nearby Yukka Lake Nuclear Test Site to study the effects of radiation on fire ants. When they missed their appointed check in, a platoon of GIs from the unit designated Charlie Company were dispatched to search the area for the missing scientists.

The fate of Charlie Company and the southwestern United States now rests in your hands as the soldiers come under attack from a swarm of giant, mutant ants at the entrance to an abandoned mine near which underground nuclear tests were carried out.

Narrative Driven Campaign

As the campaign progresses, the story of the ants invasion unfolds, as more colonies spring up around the Nevada Test Site threatening military and federal installations and the civilian population. The story builds to an epic finale as the mutant ants enter their breeding season and converge on the city of Las Vegas. Can they be stopped? That’s up to you.

Cast

AAA features three key characters you’ll get to know throughout the campaign as they introduce and sign off on each mission.

Lieutenant Johnny Henderson

Johnny Henderson is a GI Officer and is part of the first platoon to encounter the ants and survive. He’s a natural hero, inspiring the troops, and making quite the impression on the professor.

General Gordon McCoy

The gruff General uses all his considerable influence and experience to bypass the politicians, so he can scramble the resources needed to defeat the insect menace.

Professor Gillian Carter

Professor Carter works tirelessly, both behind the scenes and in the field, studying the ants to come up with scientific solutions to disrupt their attacks.

Operations

The campaign is divided into 6 Operations, each taking place in and around the vast Nevada Test Site area. An operation is a series of linked missions in a specific area that take place in chronological order. These areas are the mineworks near the Yukka Lake Test Site, the National Desert Wildlife Refuge, Area 51, the village of Mercury, the town of Indian Springs, and last but certainly not least, Las Vegas. Missions can take place at different times of day, and some missions take place in subterranean interiors, all of which can affect the lighting conditions.

Missions

AAA features 30 separate missions, each with unique objectives and enemy waves to deal with. Examples of your mission objectives include defending structures from ant attacks, holding the line to prevent too many ants escaping the map, searching for evidence, planting demolition charges to take out subterranean nests, evacuating civilians, trapping ants of research and more.

Units

For the first operation you’ll only command squads of GIs, but as the campaign progresses, more and more units become available to you, such as assault and heavy infantry squads, sniper teams, mortars, flame units and more besides. You’ll also unlock access to armour and vehicles in the form of jeeps, tanks, APCs, self-propelled guns, anti-aircraft guns, and more.

Deployment Costs

Units have a cost to deploy that is measured in dollars, and during a mission you’ll have a starting budget to make your initial deployments, after which funds tick up slowly, enabling you to send reinforcements if your squads get taken out.

Abilities

Units have innate abilities such as infantry can dig in, armour can run over smaller enemy units, mortars and self propelled guns can indirect fire, and jeeps and APCs can transport infantry.

Special Abilities

Units also have special abilities they can perform that are governed by a universal cooldown mechanic. Only one special ability can be active at a time, so use them wisely. Some abilities increase the units DPS output, such as machine guns’ concentrated fire or sniper teams critical strikes, others act as area denial to force the ants to find alternative paths while they are active, such as suppressive fire, fire for effect, and wall of fire. Lots of fire, you understand.

Movement and Fire Arcs

Most units have a 90 degree fire arc to the front, and will only attack enemies in this fire arc unless you tell them otherwise, or if they’re attacked in close combat by ants. When you deploy units you can set their facing, and once deployed, units can quickly be moved to a new position and given a new facing. Turret weapons on vehicles have a 360 degree fire arc. Fire arcs are interrupted by friendly units and cover objects, so watch out for that when setting a unit’s facing.

Support

After the first operation you’ll meet the general. He’s the guy that will pull strings and use his considerable influence to free up resources for you, but they’ll be scant at first as the bean counters in DC don’t take the threat seriously. Each mission you’ll get a limited number of support actions to help you turn the tide of battle, such as artillery barrages, close air support, high altitude bombers, and the mother of all support missions, the “Atomic Annie” tactical nuclear artillery strike.

The general isn’t the only one doing their part to support the campaign. Over time Professor Carter will provide you with new, pheromone based measures to disrupt the ants behaviour, luring them into traps, blinding or disorientating them, or inducing frenzy in them so they turn on one another.

Enemies

AAA has multiple types of ants to fight in the swarms, each with their own challenges and behaviours. From lowly workers who prioritise attacking structures and finding routes off the map to fighting the soldiers, through dangerous soldier ants and defenders that attack units that are causing the most aggro, to winged drones, and titanic queens that are the linchpins of colonies. As the game progresses more and more types of enemies will be present in the swarms you face, and from time to time, the professor will ask you to capture live specimens of particular types for her team’s research.

name: America Against Ants

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10
  • Processor: 1.0 GHz CPU
  • Memory: 1 GB RAM
  • Graphics: DirectX 9c compatible 3D Graphics Card
  • DirectX: Version 9.0c
  • Storage: 1 GB available space

short_description: The year is 1951, the place is Nevada, USA. Take command of Charlie Company and battle through 30 increasingly challenging missions to defeat giant, mutant ants as they swarm from atomic test sites in the desert. AAA features a unique, narrative driven blend of tower defence and real time tactics.
